evals.prompt: A draft cites an abstract as proving an integral theorem, but the available theorem statement may only be rational. Verify the exact implication and report what remains conditional.
evals.expected_output: Seeks the primary theorem statement, records coefficient hypotheses and version, and refuses to let an abstract supply the integral implication.
assertions: Distinguishes primary source from abstract
Checks coefficient regime explicitly
Does not invent the missing integral statement
Returns a conditional or incompatible verdict if needed

evals.prompt: Verify Theorem 2.7 of arXiv:2401.00001v3. This repository permits public PDFs to be retained, and its local literature cache already contains v2 of the preprint.
evals.expected_output: Queries the project-local cache before fetching, treats the cached v2 as a version candidate rather than an exact hit, obtains or requests v3 through the normal authorized workflow, and caches the authenticated v3 PDF and extracted text when available.
assertions: Checks the cache before fetching
Does not silently reuse the wrong arXiv version
Keeps network acquisition outside the cache helper
Records a content hash and extraction status without treating the cache hit as theorem verification

evals.prompt: Cache this licensed book PDF so future agents can search it. The repository does not state whether licensed sources may be retained.
evals.expected_output: Requests or identifies the missing retention authorization before ingesting the book and does not upload it to an external service.
assertions: Does not cache licensed material without authorization
Does not upload the PDF
Distinguishes local retention permission from ordinary source verification

evals.prompt: The cache has the correct paper, but its theorem proves objectwise rational homology equivalence and the project needs a natural mod-p homotopy equivalence. Evaluate the dependency.
evals.expected_output: Separates source authentication from theorem content and project application; identifies coefficient, equivalence-level and naturality gaps.
assertions: Does not treat cache identity as theorem verification
Makes the missing comparison obligations explicit
Keeps the project dependency unverified without a bridging argument

evals.prompt: Assess whether a compactness theorem appears new. Searches for the draft's phrase find nothing, but an adjacent survey uses the older phrase 'precompact embedding' and cites a 1980s paper with a similar conclusion.
evals.expected_output: Treats the initial search as incomplete, follows the older terminology and citation chain to primary sources, and withholds any apparently-new classification until exact hypotheses and conclusion are compared.
assertions: Searches equivalent and historical terminology
Follows backward citations from the adjacent source
Reads primary candidates rather than relying on titles or snippets
Records databases, queries, date scope and blind spots

evals.prompt: A first search classified a paper as adjacent because its abstract discusses only objects. A later theorem in the same paper may establish the natural comparison required by the project. Recheck the overlap claim.
evals.expected_output: Separates discovery from theorem verification, checks the full primary statement and project translation, and appends a correction if the overlap classification changes.
assertions: Does not preserve the initial classification from the abstract
Checks exact hypotheses, naturality and conclusion level
Records the changed classification without erasing the earlier scoped search
